summary:
North Carolina stands under the United States framework, and national rules on passports, entry screening, federal custody and federal health funding apply in the state as they do elsewhere in the country. The state layer is where the facility, identification, care and bias-crime questions are decided.

Facility rules are the subject of live legislative conflict rather than settled prohibition. House Bill 2, passed in an emergency 2016 session after the Charlotte city council allowed transgender people to use facilities matching their gender identity, required public bathroom use according to the sex listed on a birth certificate and barred cities from enacting anti-discrimination ordinances covering gay and transgender people. The birth-certificate bathroom provision was repealed by the General Assembly on 30 March 2017, and no state statute now bars a trans person from using the facility matching their gender identity, nor criminalises facility use. Republican legislators revived a bathroom bill in the 2025 session, so the position remains open and could change within a legislative term.

Identification documents are narrowing. A federal ruling of 26 June 2022 removed the undefined sex-reassignment-surgery requirement from the state's birth-certificate amendment process after Lambda Legal's November 2021 suit. House Bill 805, enacted over veto on 29 July 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, recognises only male and female sexes and requires an amended certificate to keep displaying the sex originally assigned alongside any change, which means a corrected state document still carries the original marker.

Care for minors is closed. Three veto-overridden laws effective 16 August 2023 ended the prescription of puberty blockers and hormone therapy and the provision of gender-affirming surgery to people under 18, and House Bill 574 barred individuals assigned male at birth from female sports and athletic teams. House Bill 805 additionally bars state funds for gender-transition care for minors and for people in prison, so a trans visitor held in state custody would not obtain transition care at state expense. A trans athlete visiting or competing in the state falls under the sports restriction.

Recourse after violence is limited. The state hate-crime statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so an assault on a trans visitor may not be charged as a bias crime under state law even where bias is evident.

Non-discrimination coverage outside public employment is municipal and county-level. A state prohibition on local ordinances covering gender identity expired on 1 December 2020; Charlotte and Wake County ordinances explicitly covering gender identity took effect 1 January 2022, and roughly 30 per cent of the state's population lives under a local ordinance covering sexual orientation and gender identity. A trans visitor therefore has no statewide protection in private employment, housing or public accommodations, and the answer depends on the particular city or county.
tangentialFactors:
House Bill 2 produced a commercial and legal conflict that outlasted the law itself: companies including Google and Disney pledged to pull back business from the state, the U.S. Justice Department called the law state-sponsored discrimination and sued, North Carolina filed its own suit, and the legislature repealed the measure on 30 March 2017.

North Carolina G.S. 14-177 remains on the statute book. After Lawrence v. Texas (2003) it is unenforceable for private consensual adult conduct, and State v. Whiteley (2005) upheld it on its face only for minors, non-consensual or coercive conduct, public conduct, and prostitution. A trans visitor in a relationship that state law would read through birth-sex status faces no live exposure under it, but the provision has not been repealed.

A federal judge in January 2021 struck down the state's exclusion of couples it classified as same-sex from domestic-violence protection, extending the protective-order framework to them. A 2008 patients' bill of rights provision grants hospital visitation through a designated-visitor statute.
localsOnly:
Students are governed directly by the 2023 school laws. Senate Bill 49, the Parents' Bill of Rights, took effect 15 August 2023: it bars instruction on gender identity in kindergarten through fourth grade, requires school personnel to notify a parent if a student requests a different name or pronoun in records or in class, and gives parents inspection and objection rights over instructional materials.

Public employment protections for residents rest on an executive order of 12 April 2016 barring discrimination against LGBT state employees, including on gender identity, and an October 2017 extension covering state contractors. The University of North Carolina system and most of its campuses maintain gender-identity non-discrimination policies for employment and for students.

Conversion therapy on minors may not be state-funded under an executive order of 3 August 2019. A law signed in November 2021 and effective 1 January 2022 bans sexual-orientation discrimination in foster-parenting placements.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether trans residents face lethal violence at a rate above the state's general homicide rate is not established by the sources available here, and no comparison should be inferred from published counts for the state.

The text, coverage and current status of the bathroom bill introduced in the 2025 session are not established by the sources, nor is any enforcement practice by local law enforcement at facilities.

It is not established how county registers of deeds are applying the requirement that an amended birth certificate continue to display the sex originally assigned, or whether that display affects driver's licence issuance.

The 30 per cent figure for local ordinance coverage is a share of population rather than of territory, so it does not tell a visitor whether a given city or county has an ordinance covering gender identity.
